messages:
maria.g: Heads up — saw multiple customer tickets this morning where a single org's burst ate our shared capacity and pushed p95 latencies up 2x for others. Thinking we need "per-org smoothing" + noisy-neighbor detection. Any objections to a design doc?

kevin.t: +1 to doc. real quick Q: are we aiming for hard per-org token buckets or a soft smoothing layer (EWMA) on top of the global rate limiter?

sophie.k: Soft smoothing would be less surprising to customers; hard buckets are easier to reason about for billing. We should consider hybrid: per-org reservoir + short-term smoothing window.

aj: Hybrid sounds right. Proposed model: per-org leaky bucket for steady-state (tokens/sec) + a small burst reservoir that refills slowly. Add EWMA to scale down effective burst when we detect tail lat spikes across peers.

maria.g: +1. Need to define detection: noisy neighbor = org whose p95 latency > cluster_p95 * 1.5 AND error rate or cpu/gpu saturation correlates. If detected, automatically throttle their burst to conserve fairness.

kevin.t: Implementation notes: currently we have per-key ratelimit middleware in nginx/edge and a centralized limiter service. Which layer should enforce smoothing?

sophie.k: Centralized limiter service — easier to coordinate across replicas and to emit metrics. Edge should still apply guardrails (absolute hard cap) to prevent weird traffic shaping.

aj: Telemetry we need: per-org token_consumption_rate, burst_exhaustions, enforced_smoothing_count, p95_latency_org, cpu_util_org (approx). Also traces to link request families so we can root-cause heavy batch jobs.

observability-bot: New metric set proposed: org.rate.tokens_per_minute, org.rate.burst_remaining, org.latency.p95, org.saturation.gpu_util. — Will create metric templates if you +1.

maria.g: +1 from product. UX asks: in Console, show current smoothing status and a 24h timeline of burst events per org and a one-click "request burst override" for SRE-approved emergencies.

kevin.t: For rollout: feature flag per_org_smoothing_v1 behind kill-switch. Canary on 5% of orgs (random stable sample) for 48hrs then 25% then full. Also add a rollback job to revert quota changes per-customer.

sophie.k: We should also add an experiment to compare hybrid vs pure-leaky-bucket: A/B two cohorts and measure downstream p95 impact and customer error rates.

aj: Perf details: smoothing window 30s EWMA alpha=0.3 as default, burst reservoir size default 2x steady_rate but configurable. Example config snippet: 
```
org_quota: 
  steady_rate: 10/s
  burst_capacity: 20
  smoothing: 
    window_s: 30
    alpha: 0.3
``` 

maria.g: Looks good. Also add billing signal: if burst > X we mark as billable overage and notify billing console. Product wants opt-in for paid burst.

kevin.t: One more: we need a cheap detector to mark "noisy" before metrics pipeline aggregates. Maybe a p99 short-window counter from envoy or edge (10s window) to immediately apply emergency smoothing.

sophie.k: Agree. Edge can emit a small telemetry side-channel to limiter. We'll keep it limited to counts (requests, errors, token usage) to avoid perf hit.

maria.g: Action items: 1) @kevin.t to draft design doc with architecture (central limiter + edge guardrail + detectors) by EOD Friday. 2) @aj to prototype smoothing algorithm in limiter and add metric emissions (tokens, burst_exhaust) — 1 week. 3) @sophie.k to mock console UX and billing integration — 1 week. 4) add canary plan and experiment matrix.

kevin.t: I'll start doc. Quick question about naming: call the feature "per-org smoothing" in config but Console label "Fairness smoothing"? Thoughts?

sophie.k: Console label should be plain: "Traffic fairness" or "Fairness smoothing" — product will A/B test text. "Traffic fairness" might be clearer for non-technical users.

aj: FYI for implementation: we'll need to update rate-limiter-binary to persist per-org reservoir state to Redis (leaky buckets need a durable last-timestamp). That will require a schema bump. I'll add compatibility notes in the PR.

rate-limiter-bot: Reminder: existing rate-limiter schema migration window is 2 weeks. Plan migrations accordingly.

maria.g: Thanks all. If no blockers I want this prioritized for the next infra sprint. Posting link to rough notes: https://docs.internal/research/fairness-smoothing-draft (internal) :wave:

kevin.t: ACK — will drop a first pass this afternoon.

sophie.k: I'll start Console mocks after lunch.

aj: Prototype branch will be up by EOD Tuesday.

maria.g: Closing loop — please add yourselves to the doc authors list and tag any customers for whom this might change SLAs.

observability-bot: Created dashboard template: "org-fairness-overview". Link: https://observability/dashboards/org-fairness-overview

kevin.t: Great, thanks.

maria.g: End of thread.
